title: Hold a run until its route can answer input
description: A route of a run the daemon accepted could not answer at the submit: the gateway is ready and lists the alias, and the status of the model (`callable` of `GET /v1/status`, else the phase of `GET /v1/models/{alias}/status` for a managed or a local route) says it cannot take a call now. The run is WaitingForRoute: no call goes to the route, and nothing is woken unless the route is managed with its wake on (`wake_on_submit`, accepted at start only with `wake_daily_cap_micro_usd` and `wake_cost_micro_usd` above 0): a model the gateway gave as `stopped` then gets one `POST /v1/models/{alias}/wake` for the run before the first read of the wait, booked first, under the lock of the state, in the run event `runbook.route-wake` (record: route, sent, day, cost_micro_usd, booked_micro_usd, cap_micro_usd; a wake the rest of the route's cap for the day of the daemon's clock does not cover is not sent, `sent` false and reason `wake cap reached`; a run less than the route's `start_wait_seconds` after a wake sent for the same route by any run joins that wake: nothing is sent or booked, `sent` false, reason `joined a wake sent within the wait`, and `joined` and `joined_at` name the run and the instant of that wake), and the gateway's answer is the run event `runbook.route-wake-answered` (record: route, status, and code when the gateway gave one); an answer `spend-ceiling` ends the run (EndRouteWait). The daemon reads the status at most once every 5 seconds of its clock, up to the least `start_wait_seconds` of the routes that cannot answer (none declared: no wait); once every route of the run can answer, the runtime starts it (StartRun); past the wait the daemon ends it (EndRouteWait). The daemon also writes the run event `runbook.waiting-for-route` (record: route, phase, wait_seconds); see CancelRun for why it is stated here. Issued by the daemon itself (actor DaemonProcess): it has no route in the HTTP contract.

phase.description: The phase the gateway gave of the route's model.

sdc.daemon.RunId.title: RunId
sdc.daemon.RunId.description: The id of a run. The daemon mints it (a UUID, version 7) in the HTTP handler and returns it in the answer to the submit; the handler fills the `run_id` input of SubmitRun and a client never chooses it. The state directory of the run is named after it. A run id that is already taken cannot occur, because the daemon mints it; the specification has no refusal for it.
